hey team - my initial thoughts:


----


*T&Cs set-up:*Regarding T&Cs going forward, for each market we’ll have ‘*one set*’ of T&Cs that apply equally to ‘*service providers*’ that offer and charge passengers for services, whether that’s:
(*A*) a service provider that charges passengers *who is an individual acting on his/her own behalf*

(*B*) a service provider that charges passengers *which is a fleet (that onboards fleet drivers to fulfil rides on behalf of the fleet)*_(We will not have a set of terms that applies directly to ‘fleet drivers that are onboarded by a fleet’ <--- this includes 'substitutes' who are the same for contractual purposes)_


----


*The Product Team Question:*

In respect of *(B)*, there is not an obvious need to limit information - of course a 'fleet service provider' should see various info etc. of the fleet drivers that are providing work on their behalf.The issue is therefore mostly in relation to (A): a 'service provider that charges passengers who is an individual' rents a car from a fleet. The product team want to know whether it's necessary to limit the flow of data to this fleet.I presume we can do whatever we want so long as it's recorded in our privacy notice for the market, BUT as a point of commercial principle: *why would/should Bolt be sharing (A)'s payment/geolocation information with a rental company like this?*  Has this commercial rationale been outlined anywhere....? 

Regardless, we presumably can't do it unless it's set out in our privacy policy and we're making it very clear to drivers that this info is being shared. If it IS set out in our privacy policy and you're happy with it, then that's generally fine by me.

[~accountid:712020:f63df97f-cad1-4718-9bb1-80038488d7e2] [~accountid:62134a797580350068337097] As discussed with Liisa, there are two main intellectual property (IP) risks involved when gathering large scale market intelligence data:

# infringement of trade secrets - collecting and storing the data about a competitor’s business over a long time period may create a situation where the data constitutes a competitor's trade secret, which as a whole is not publicly available; 
# Infringement of database rights - collecting and storing the data over a long time period may lead to copying of a competitor’s database (e.g. prices and partners).

The fact that individual items of the data are publicly available does not exclude the risk of IP infringement. The risk arises primarily due to a set of data (not public as a whole) obtained as a result of long-term automated data collection. The court practice in data scraping disputes is inconsistent, but there have been cases where courts have found that the fact that the data is taken from a publicly accessible website does not mean its scraping is legal. 

The following measures may help to lower the risk of IP infringement claims:

* Scale and frequency on an actual need basis: 
** Need-based: e.g. when forming, reviewing, changing our pricing strategy. 
** Reactive: e.g. when competitor adjust their pricing strategy;
** Periodical: what is the reasoning for the biweekly reporting frequency? Why not monthly?
* Periodic deletion of data. In addition to limiting the quantity of data that will be scraped, it is also important to limit the quantity of data that will be kept. It may be difficult to escape from liability and, from the other side, it is more easier for competitors to prove that their database was copied, if all data is kept and never deleted.  
* Ownership of data vs license to use. Do we need to own the data or is it sufficient if it is stored by a third party service provider and we have an access? Using third party services inserts a distance between the data and Bolt. Competitors have an additional burden of proof to attribute infringing activity to Bolt. The license may also serve as a mechanism to transfer risk to a third party - pricing service with a risk-premium in return for not accepting liability shift.

Best,

Indrek

Hello [~accountid:6411c587f1b529dfa98c0e66] , 

I see three different sub-topics: 

# *Appointing a statutory auditor* for the next 6 years ASAP. 
# *Arranging required corporate documents and submit them to the interim relief judge* to regularize the situation since we are beyond the deadline for the appointment (31/12/2023). OC needs to know the name of the appointed statutory auditor to draft the required documents. 
# *Approving FY2023 financials by June 2024* or consider asking for an extension (OC can help with that) if we think that the statutory auditor won’t be appointed on time and won’t be able to review the financials by then. 
# *Discussing about filing financials*  which for me is not very urgent an as highlighted again by OC “_Some companies opt not to file their accounts_ +*_without_*+ _immediate and serious consequence (in case they receive an injunction from the Commercial court to file their accounts, they will have a sometime to proceed)”._ Filing financials might entail additional external counsel fees and in the past the Business decided not to file to preserve confidentiality. My understanding from OC replies is that OC FR has the obligation to appoint a statutory auditor regardless of whether we are filing financials. 

My understanding from OC note is the *likelihood of facing penalties for not filing is minimal*, and we will have an opportunity to rectify the non-compliance upon receiving a formal injunction to comply. 

However, *failure to appoint the* +*statutory auditor*+ *carries heavier consequences, punishable under* +*criminal law with up to 2 years' imprisonment and a fine of €30,000.*+ 

Given these risks, the *primary focus* should be on appointing the statutory auditor and progressing with above tasks No. 1 and 2. Additionally, it may be prudent to request an extension for approving the 2023 financials and arranging for their audit by the statutory auditor concurrently. 

Also speaking with [~accountid:5b76bc2cb974540708ee16ee] early this week, he mentioned that we might face some dawn raids from the FR Tax Authority if we don’t comply asap with our obligations and this would not been the first time. 

[~accountid:610279973900e60070a3495c] , it is regrettable that the local accountant who prepared the balance sheet did not flag the fact that in 2022 we reached the thresholds triggering the obligations to appoint a statutory auditor. Though, local accountant might help to source and appoint statutory auditor ( “_Commissaire aux comptes_”). [~accountid:610279973900e60070a3495c] Would you be able to liaise with your local partner and assist on the matter?

Findings so far:
This issue occurs when:
1) scaling down STS replicas and back up again
2) draining nodes

Does not occur during rolling update.

Noted that when scaling down or draining nodes, the PVCs for no-longer existent pods remain bound to non-existent nodes. Force deleting the PVCs then allows for the STS to be scaled up successfully on new nodes.

{noformat}spec:

    whenScaled: Delete{noformat}

Hey [~accountid:5da9bc834ebac20c36a35aa3] let me first try to explain how the bonuses work within Billing for more context but let me know if there’s anything unclear

First of all in Bolt we have 2 different client/entity types in Rides → Drivers & Fleets (& Fleet Drivers) 
In Billing this is very important because in our eyes Drivers are drivers with driver-based invoicing. These drivers have their own balance, payouts go directly to the driver, invoices are issued to the driver etc. Fleets (& Fleet Drivers) are drivers with company-based invoicing. These drivers DO NOT have their own balance as everything they earn is moved to the fleet balance. Payouts & invoices go to the fleet (Fleet Owner) who then is required to pay their drivers etc.

Hence in the query below we have 2 breakdowns → Fleet based bonuses & Driver based bonuses

----

Next we migrated the balances over to RHv2 [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/4778033478/Rides+Balance+Migration+from+invoicing2+to+RHB|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/4778033478/Rides+Balance+Migration+from+invoicing2+to+RHB|smart-link] in end 2022 / start 2023. Basically what this means data-wise we now have visibility on transaction-level data vs in the past (called _invoicing_) we aggregated everything daily. 

As Rides balance data is used a lot externally, in Billing Analytics we migrated the main balance tables over to RHv2 as well. For example:

* We had a table called {{ng_public.invoicing_campaign_bonus}} -> this is the source of truth for campaign bonuses when the old system (invoicing) was active
* After RHv2 was launched all transactions started flowing into {{ng_public.billing_ride_hailing_record}} table ->  this is the source of truth for campaign bonuses (and any other transaction type) in the new system (RHv2) 
* As record level data is pretty complex to normalise we created an ETL called {{ng_public.etl_billing_balance_campaign_bonus}} which joins data from both sources ^^ and normalises it to have the continuous data flow & helps making the migrations as smooth as possible for external users. More details in the Confluence above

Now this leaves us the daily aggregates of campaign bonuses for the end users → Drivers & Fleets but we are still missing campaign bonuses breakdown for Fleet Drivers (who don’t actually get anything because everything is automatically moved to the Fleet’s balance right). To still see the Fleet Driver level breakdown we can use 

* {{ng_public.invoicing_campaign_bonus_data}} -> this is the source of truth for campaign bonuses for Fleet Drivers when the old system (invoicing) was active
* {{ng_public.etl_billing_balance_campaign_bonus_details}} -> this is the transaction level source of truth for campaign bonuses for Fleet Drivers (and Drivers & Fleets) when RHv2 is active

Hence in the query below we have 3 different subqueries per bonus type to show the full overview of driver bonuses:

* Legacy Fleet Driver bonus → period when old system / invoicing was active. e.g. data coming from {{invoicing_campaign_bonus_data}} table

Example query:

{noformat}select 
'legacy_fleet_campaign_bonus' as bonus_type,
cb.currency,
cb.compensation_fee_type,
cb.compensation_fee_subtype,
cbd.external_id as driver_id,
cb.date as created_date,
sum(cbd.sum_with_vat) as total_driver_bonus
from ng_public.etl_billing_balance_campaign_bonus cb
left join ng_public.invoicing_campaign_bonus_data cbd on cbd.campaign_bonus_id = cb.id and cb.source = 'invoicing' and cb.entity_type = 'fleet'
where cb.entity_type = 'fleet' --> to include only bonuses for fleets (fleet drivers)
and cb.source = 'invoicing' --> only from legacy source
and cbd.sum_with_vat is not null --> excldude bonuses directly to the fleet
and cb.date >= DATE('2022-04-01') and cb.date < DATE('2022-05-01') --> date in local time 
group by 1,2,3,4,5,6{noformat}

* New Fleet Driver bonus → period when new system / RHv2 is active. e.g. data coming from {{etl_billing_balance_campaign_bonus_details}} table

Example query:

{noformat}select 
'new_fleet_campaign_bonus' as bonus_type,
currency,
compensation_fee_type,
compensation_fee_subtype,
driver_id,
date as created_date,
sum(sum_with_vat) as total_driver_bonus
from ng_public.etl_billing_balance_campaign_bonus_details 
where entity_type = 'fleet' --> include only bonuses to fleets (fleet drivers)
and driver_id is not null  --> exclude bonuses directly to the fleet
and date >= DATE('2024-04-01') and date < DATE('2024-05-01') --> date in local time
group by 1,2,3,4,5,6{noformat}

* (Private) Driver bonus → full history. e.g. data coming from {{etl_billing_balance_campaign_bonus}} table

Example query:

{noformat}select distinct 
'driver_campaign_bonus' as bonus_type,
currency,
compensation_fee_type,
compensation_fee_subtype,
entity_id as driver_id,
date as created_date,
sum_with_vat as total_driver_bonus
from ng_public.etl_billing_balance_campaign_bonus 
where entity_type = 'driver' --> only (private) drivers
and date >= DATE('2024-04-01') and date < DATE('2024-05-01') --> date in local time{noformat}

----

Finally, in Billing we have 3 different bonus types we process:

* Campaign Bonuses → automatic bonuses we cannot invoice separately
* Manual Compensations → manual bonuses (via manual adjustments) we cannot invoice separately
* Compensations → automatic & manual bonuses we CAN invoice separately (invoice requirement = driver/fleet legal type = Business)

Hence in the query below we have further 3 breakdown - campaign bonuses, manual comps & comps 

----

Now putting everything together: 

{noformat}with summary as (
/* 
### Campaign Bonuses ###
###### Legacy Fleet ######
*/
select 
'legacy_fleet_campaign_bonus' as bonus_type,
cb.currency,
cb.compensation_fee_type,
cb.compensation_fee_subtype,
cbd.external_id as driver_id,
cb.date as created_date,
sum(cbd.sum_with_vat) as total_driver_bonus
from ng_public.etl_billing_balance_campaign_bonus cb
left join ng_public.invoicing_campaign_bonus_data cbd on cbd.campaign_bonus_id = cb.id and cb.source = 'invoicing' and cb.entity_type = 'fleet'
where cb.entity_type = 'fleet' --> to include only bonuses for fleets (fleet drivers)
and cb.source = 'invoicing' --> only from legacy source
and cbd.sum_with_vat is not null --> excldude bonuses directly to the fleet
group by 1,2,3,4,5,6
union all
/*
###### New Fleet ###### 
*/
select 
'new_fleet_campaign_bonus' as bonus_type,
currency,
compensation_fee_type,
compensation_fee_subtype,
driver_id,
date as created_date,
sum(sum_with_vat) as total_driver_bonus
from ng_public.etl_billing_balance_campaign_bonus_details 
where entity_type = 'fleet' --> include only bonuses to fleets (fleet drivers)
and driver_id is not null  --> exclude bonuses directly to the fleet
group by 1,2,3,4,5,6
union all 
/*
###### (Private) Driver ###### 
*/
select distinct 
'driver_campaign_bonus' as bonus_type,
currency,
compensation_fee_type,
compensation_fee_subtype,
entity_id as driver_id,
date as created_date,
sum_with_vat as total_driver_bonus
from ng_public.etl_billing_balance_campaign_bonus 
where entity_type = 'driver' --> only (private) drivers
union all
/*
### Compensations ###
###### Legacy Fleet ###### 
*/
select 
'legacy_fleet_compensation' as bonus_type,
c.currency,
c.compensation_fee_type,
c.compensation_fee_subtype,
cd.external_id as driver_id,
c.date as created_date,
sum(cd.sum_with_vat) as total_driver_bonus
from ng_public.etl_billing_balance_compensation c
left join ng_public.invoicing_compensation_data cd on cd.compensation_id = c.id and c.source = 'invoicing' and c.entity_type = 'fleet'
where c.entity_type = 'fleet' --> to include only compensations for fleets (fleet drivers)
and c.source = 'invoicing' --> only from legacy source
and cd.sum_with_vat is not null --> excldude bonuses directly to the fleet
group by 1,2,3,4,5,6
union all
/*
###### New Fleet ###### 
*/
select 
'new_fleet_compensation' as bonus_type,
currency,
compensation_fee_type,
compensation_fee_subtype,
driver_id,
date as created_date,
sum(sum_with_vat) as total_driver_bonus
from ng_public.etl_billing_balance_compensation_details  
where entity_type = 'fleet' --> include only bonuses to fleets (fleet drivers)
and driver_id is not null  --> exclude bonuses directly to the fleet
group by 1,2,3,4,5,6
union all
/*
###### (Private) Driver ###### 
*/
select distinct 
'driver_compensation' as bonus_type,
currency,
compensation_fee_type,
compensation_fee_subtype,
entity_id as driver_id,
date as created_date,
sum_with_vat as total_driver_bonus
from ng_public.etl_billing_balance_compensation  
where entity_type = 'driver' --> only (private) drivers
union all
/*
### Manual Compensations ###

*/

After reviewing everything I could find, here are some points to think about when it comes to the voice messages users can leave:

* The voice message feature is intended to serve as a way of reporting badly parked scooters. When the user calls us, they hear a voice message asking to let us know about an incorrectly parked rental and that they need to send us an in-app message if the issue is about something else. To my knowledge, majority of these voice messages are exactly that - reports of badly parked scooters, and these kind of reports do not require any direct interaction with the user as we just need to locate the scooter and mark it for collection in our system. If the person has a different issue, they need to reach out to us via the app or email. 
* Escalation to Tier 2 is not necessary as badly parked scooter cases are solved by Tier 1.
* An outgoing call to the user could be a solution, however, since we have markets where the CS agents do not speak the local language, unfortunately, implementing such a process step would not be possible at the moment.
* If the reporter is a third party without an account with Bolt, we don’t have any means to identify the person, even if their question is specific, e.g. a lost item or anything else, so the support we could provide is very limited and either way the person would need to be re-directed to the app/email.

Hey, [~accountid:712020:79bdda29-2f20-4318-9d05-92c9d0bd7b47]! 

This issue is not specific to localisation freelancers. The problem is that when we conclude a contract with a private person who is not self-employed or not acting on behalf of a company, we help people to evade taxes and this is not something we would like to do as an organisation. In Croatia people can easily register themselves as self-employed or establish this “small craft business” (OBRT).

Regarding the platforms you referred to ([useme.com|http://useme.com/] and [+Xolo.io+|http://xolo.io/]) - it all depends on how these persons use these companies:

* If freelancers use these companies’ ([useme.com|http://useme.com/] and [+Xolo.io+|http://xolo.io/]) invoicing software and produce invoices on behalf of themselves (or freelancer’s company) - this is fine as long as the person is registered as a self-employed or invoice is issued by the company or OBRT of the person who performed the service. If the invoice they issue is issued by them in the capacity of a private person that is not self-employed, then even though the invoice itself will be ok - we cannot sign a contract with them because as explained earlier, the freelancer needs to have a company, OBRT or be self-employed.
* If these companies ([useme.com|http://useme.com/] and [+Xolo.io+|http://xolo.io/]) are the ones who issue the invoice (i.e. act as a beneficiary of the money to be received) then this is not acceptable, because the invoice has to be issued by a person (or a company) who performed the service.

In order to sign a contract with a freelancer and receive an invoice from them these conditions need to be satisfied:

# The freelancer needs to be either self-employed or have an OBRT or a company.
# The invoice needs to be issued by the person (if self-employed) or a company/OBRT that actually performed the service.

Please do not hesitate to reach out if you have any further question.

🚨 It’s difficult to estimate or quantify the impact and probability of risk realisation which Indrek brought out, since there is limited case law on this. However, we are seeing the tendency from our competitors side as well as in general, that companies are regulating data scraping on their T&Cs, by directly or indirectly prohibiting it (including Bolt). 

*Risks are  even higher if:* 

# *scraped data is non-public, meaning*: (i) prohibited in the T&Cs, (ii) log-in is needed to access the data and if supplier (data scraper) will do it unethically
# *if the supplier shares files with Bolt which Bolt can copy, save or store in its systems.* 

*In order to mitigate the risks we have:*

# pushed all the liability in relation to potential third party claims in relation to actual or alleged infringement of any third party’s IPRs to the supplier. Whether the supplier agrees to it, is up to negotiations. +We should push for it strongly.+
# obliged the supplier to only do ethical scraping (not mentioning scraping expressly ofc) and to give an confirmation that all the data which supplier shares is obtained legally: “_The Supplier confirms that any data or information used for offering Services for Bolt are obtained legally and in an ethical manner (including towards third parties if relevant) by not damaging or interfering third parties rights (including IPRs) or property (tangible or intangible).”_
# obliged the supplier to “_remove Bolt’s access to or delete data it has shared with Bolt as a part of Services from supplier’s systems if this data is related to third party business operating models directly or indirectly, after three (3) months of termination or expiry of this Agreement Term_.” 

Basically even if one of our competitors should claim the the supplier scraped for us, then this regulation here should make it harder to prove it due to fact the supplier doesn’t have this data in their systems (provided that supplier indeed deletes this data). However, since we mention this in the contract then this still indicates that we have asked the supplier to scrape the data + in reality court always looks at the factual situation. Meaning if Bolt is obliged to show what kind of data we have on our systems and we have stored it and not deleted it +after it is not commercially imperative (see Indrek notes)+, then it is quite easy to count Bolt liable for third party IPRs infringement.

Context dump after a chat with [~accountid:557058:45102889-d5d0-4b8f-9a89-5fc4235fa2ce] 

There’s a hierarchy of Engineering teams, with each mapping to its own cost center, which is used from multiple places. The hierarchy is as follows:

* on the top there are verticals
* verticals consist of groups
* groups consist of teams
* each team has its own cost center

You can check this spreadsheet for more details: [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1xfHc_obwWe9kBqVaV-xnBa4Batef8rvSwdyEcTUGzpg/edit?usp=sharing|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1xfHc_obwWe9kBqVaV-xnBa4Batef8rvSwdyEcTUGzpg/edit?usp=sharing|smart-link] You can see that sometimes the group is missing and a team belongs directly to a vertical.

The ask is to have such hierarchy available for managers in a centralized place, so that they could configure their teams (EMs), groups (SEMs), and verticals (directors). Right now the only metadata attached to each team is its cost center (along with the cost center owner), but there might be need for more in the future. The structure along with the metadata should be exportable in some format like CSV or JSON for further ad-hoc processing (e.g. grouping post mortems by cost center based on teams, inter-team collaboration survey, etc.).

Github as the source of truth sounds feasible, but the main concern is that there are a lot of Github teams which don’t correspond to actual Engineering teams (so called “virtual” teams), so if we stay with Github we’ll need a way to differentiate between actual teams from the organization and the rest.

The main concern from the engineering side about not having Github as the source of truth is that programmatic creation of teams in Github is right now deemed dangerous by SRE and is not allowed.

Hi Louis,

{quote}I did a search and apparently the amount received was (fare - booking fees) * commission.{quote}

This is how it is meant to be. Booking fee is a pass-through fee. It is charged from the rider by driver, but we take it back from the driver. So, technically it’s an income for Bolt - not for the driver. Driver is just the agent in between for Bolt to charge the rider for this booking fee.

If you need the driver to have this income, instead of Bolt, please drop a ticket to [https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/3/group/61/create/301|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/3/group/61/create/301|smart-link] and add the country manager as an approver. However, this is a very important pricing difference for the country, so please make sure this is approved by both Operations Manager and Country Manager. If you request this, the booking fee will be a 100% driver income (commission free).

The cited legal basis says:

Section 261 (1) In the criminal proceeding, the court, the prosecution service, and the investigating authority or, in cases specified in an Act, the organ conducting a preparatory proceeding may request any organ, legal person, or other organisation without a legal personality to provide data.

(2) After the indictment, the prosecution service may request the provision of data with a view to submitting a motion for evidence or locating or securing a means of evidence. (3) Within the framework of a data request, a) the transfer of data that is relevant to the criminal proceeding and is in the possession of the organisation, b) the transfer of electronic data or documents that are relevant to the criminal proceeding and are in the possession of the organisation, or c) the provision of information relevant to the criminal proceeding that can be provided by the organisation may be requested. (4) A data request may also be aimed at the transfer or receipt of data processed in a register of the State or a local government. (5) The following shall be specified in a data request: a) the conditions and purpose of the data request pursuant to this Act, b) data identifying the subject matter of the data request, which is required for compliance with the data request, such as, in particular, data on the person, object, or service concerned, c) the scope of data to be provided, d) the method and time limit for data provision



Section 263 (1) If permitted by an Act, an organ requesting data shall receive the necessary data by accessing the records or data files directly and may make use, for requesting data, of the assistance of the national security service designated by the Act on national security service for the performance of such services. (2) A time limit of a) at least one and up to thirty days if the data is to be provided by electronic means, b) at least eight and up to thirty days if the data is to be provided by any other means, may be set for the provision of the requested data.

After some investigation, the query probably cannot be directly optimized. The root-cause for the slow performance is that the query attempts to isolate those reactivations that have atleast one priority calculation that is less than 1 hour old. However, thousands of reactivations have thousands of priorities that need to be combed through, leading to the slow execution time.

The solution is to delete the long-persisting historic priority calculations. There doesn’t seem to be much need to be storing priority calculations for longer than 1 hour anyway.

||*Finding*||*Comment*||
|* Bolt data never leaves Slack’s infrastructure|{color:#36b37e}*This is good*{color}. It means that we don’t need to worry about Bolt data going to LLM providers like OpenAI in the USA.|
|* Bolt data is (apparently) never used to train large language models (LLMs).|{color:#36b37e}*This is good*{color}. It means that we don’t need to worry about Bolt data being used to further train the SlackAI and potentially being disclosed to other Slack customers in the future.|
|* Slack AI only works with data that members [+can already access+|https://slack.com/help/articles/360002063088-Understand-your-actions-in-Slack].|{color:#36b37e}*This is good*{color}. It means that Bolt is protected against ‘data breaches’ where one employee finds out information about another by asking the Slack AI.|
|* Slack AI upholds all of Slack’s enterprise-grade security and compliance requirements.|{color:#36b37e}*This is good*{color}. InfoSec has already approved Slack’s approach to security, so nothing has changed here.|

# Generally, in principle +*I am okay with us using SlackAI*+.
# While Slack [does not use Bolt data to train its models|https://slack.com/help/articles/28310650165907-Security-for-Slack-AI#:~:text=Customer%20data%C2%A0%20is%20never%20used%20to%20train%20large%20language%20models%20(LLMs).], I’ve read elsewhere that [we can opt-out|https://slack.com/intl/en-gb/trust/data-management/privacy-principles#:~:text=Contact%20us%20to,has%20been%20completed.] of Bolt data being used for Slack’s global models, +*so let’s please ensure that we opt-out before switching it on*+:

{quote}_Contact us to opt out. If you want to exclude your Customer Data from Slack global models, you can opt out. To opt out, please have your org, workspace owners or primary owner contact our Customer Experience team at_ [_feedback@slack.com_|mailto:feedback@slack.com] _with your workspace/org URL and the subject line ‘Slack global model opt-out request’. We will process your request and respond once the opt-out has been completed._{quote}

Hi [~accountid:610a3ee66051c5006aeeeea1] could we discuss this ticket and potential alternatives? Thank you



*BACKGROUND*

* One of the reclassification criteria in Portugal for platform workers is the exercise by the platform of labour powers, namely disciplinary power, including exclusion from future activities on the platform through account deactivation. Blocking may be therefore a reclassification criteria.
* Therefore in 2023 the internal decision was made that all automatic or statistical blocking (linked to Driver Score & Acceptance Rate) should been removed. It is no longer possible to ask a driver to retrain. The only blocking still happening relates to lack of mandatory documents, safety incidents or fraud - though a more cautious approach has been adopted there and relevant communication should be made to the fleet operators and the drivers to give them notice (when possible) and relevant explanation.
* A few months ago we implemented in PT a warning / block process for FR (finish rate) which was based on the following criteria: (a) *the driver accepts the ride*; (b) *the driver then cancels the ride* for no reason, or states it as arrived to the location and passenger is not there (when that is not the case due to geo-location review). This scenario seems to be a fraud since the driver is defrauding the expectations of the passenger and it also seems to be against the TVDE law. Consequently, it would follow under the fraud and compliance blocking reasons.

*PROPOSED PROCESS*

* Under this proposed new process Bolt would issue a warning everytime that a driver is recurrently rejecting rides. After the third consecutive warning we consider a 1 week temporary block. The process would be run by the local team and considering 30%+ rejection of rides.

*LEGAL REVIEW*

* IMO this process is not similar to the warning / block process for FR (finish rate) since the driver would be penalised for not accepting the ride. 
** Having freedom to accept the ride is important since from the one side is the only moment in time where the fleet (via its driver) has the opportunity to see the proposed price and accept it. 
** On the other side it is a demonstration of fleet (and therefore driver) *autonomy and independence*, which is a central principle to avoid reclassification. 
* Additionally, I do not think that not accepting the rides is against TVDE law. 
** This law states in article 2(3) that the provision of a TVDE service begins with the acceptance by a driver at the service of a request for transport. Therefore, the refusal of the service would appear to be right of the driver after the initial acceptance. 
** Moreover, the law provides the following reasons for refusal of transportation service:
*** Involve circulation on roads that are clearly impassable due to difficult access or in places that pose a notorious danger to the safety of the vehicle, passengers or driver;
*** Are requested by people with suspiciously dangerous behaviour;
*** Are requested in a manner incompatible with the provisions of the TVDE law.
* Overall, this process would be detrimental to Bolt in reclassification claims and would, according to the HQ analysis', potentially impact the ability to defend the currently model in -45%.
* {color:#bf2600}Potential alternatives:{color}
**

{code:sql}WITH 
count_destinations AS (
SELECT b.city_id,
b.order_id,
COUNT(*)-1 as count_of_destinations_changes
FROM ng_public.company_order_destination b
LEFT JOIN ng_public.admin_system_city sc ON b.city_id = sc.id
WHERE b.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -30, current_date) as date)																												-- DATE FILTER
--WHERE b.created_date BETWEEN date '2023-07-01' AND date '2023-08-01'																													-- DATE FILTER
AND sc.country_code = 'pl'																																								-- COUNTRY FILTER 
GROUP BY 1,2	
),
pred AS (
SELECT 
a.order_id,
a.city_id,
a.predicted_price,
a.change_reason,
row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY CAST(a.order_id as varchar)||CAST(a.city_id as varchar) ORDER BY a.created DESC) AS ROW_NUMBER_desc,
row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY CAST(a.order_id as varchar)||CAST(a.city_id as varchar) ORDER BY a.created) AS ROW_NUMBER_asc
FROM ng_public.pricing_order_prediction a 
JOIN ng_public.admin_system_city sc ON a.city_id = sc.id 
WHERE a.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -30, current_date) as date)																												-- DATE FILTER
--WHERE a.created_date BETWEEN date '2023-07-01' AND date '2023-08-01'																													-- DATE FILTER
AND sc.country_code = 'pl'																																								-- COUNTRY FILTER
)
SELECT 
TRUNCATE(CAST(p_asc.predicted_price AS double),-1) AS initial_prediction,
TRUNCATE(CAST(p_desc.predicted_price*1.00/p_asc.predicted_price AS double),1) AS predicted_price_ratio0,
APPROX_DISTINCT(co.id,0.0041) AS count_orders,
SUM(co.partner_price_eur) AS gmv_eur,
ROUND(CAST(APPROX_DISTINCT((CASE WHEN co.uncovered_amount > 0 THEN co.id END),0.0041)*1.00/APPROX_DISTINCT(co.id,0.0041) AS double),2) AS ratio_failed_payment,
SUM(co.uncovered_amount/co.eur_currency_rate) AS failed_eur
FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co
LEFT JOIN count_destinations cd ON co.order_id = cd.order_id AND co.city_id = cd.city_id 
LEFT JOIN pred p_asc ON p_asc.order_id = co.order_id AND p_asc.city_id = co.city_id AND p_asc.ROW_NUMBER_asc = 1 
LEFT JOIN pred p_desc ON p_desc.order_id = co.order_id AND p_desc.city_id = co.city_id AND p_desc.ROW_NUMBER_desc = 1 
WHERE co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -30, current_date) as date)																												-- DATE FILTER
AND co.country_code = 'pl'
AND co.order_type = 'rides'
AND co.payment_method_type LIKE '%blik%'
AND cd.count_of_destinations_changes > 0
AND TRUNCATE(CAST(p_desc.predicted_price*1.00/p_asc.predicted_price AS double),0) >= 1
AND p_asc.predicted_price >= 40
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 1,2{code}

Hi [~accountid:5aafb8a33b2fcc2a6f6bb06f], see my initial response from privacy side. 

[~accountid:612f31d89976c300693ebaf7], I will let you post your thoughts regarding the T&Cs, but I presume that any T&C-related questions should come after we answer one question - in principle, are we allowed to “expose” driver data to fleets?

To give you a bit of context, when assessing whether the privacy law allows us to do something with the data, we need to answer these questions:

* *_Why do we need this (what’s the purpose of using data in this way)?_* 
** As you said, we want this for the sake of a smooth onboarding, maintaining relations & providing pointers on the efficient work on the platform. 
*** Does this apply to all fleets?
** To me, it seems like it makes sense if we talk about traditional fleets (i.e. those who provide transportation services), but not so much when it comes to service providers that are on the Fleet Portal, but don’t provide transportation services.
* *_So, there is one very important question - what about non-traditional fleets? Does it affect them?_*
** From our perspective, it would be very hard to defend such data sharing with companies who have access to the Fleet Portal simply because they provide some sort of services, for example, they do accounting.
** Data such as blocking reasons or driver score might not be necessary for the non-traditional fleets to see.
** [~accountid:5aafb8a33b2fcc2a6f6bb06f] let us know your thoughts on this.
* *_How do we inform the drivers about it?_*
** Once we reach a decision, here is where our team jumps in - in case we reach a conclusion that it’s okay to share the data with fleets → we will make sure that the Driver Privacy Notice gives the drivers enough transparency on this. However, we need to sort out the other questions before we take this step.

Bottom line - it all comes to proportionality and necessity when we are assessing whether we can share data with a certain 3rd party.

I am more than happy to jump on a call to discuss this, if needed.

Hey [~accountid:641d5e830e6828ab20269e6d] 

Yes, we would only handle requests from *verified channels*. 

*Self-help*

Ideally, we would need a two-way verification in the Fleet Owner portal to implement the self-help solution, but unfortunately, we don’t have this option. [~accountid:61fa31c9b3ec760068c18497]might know details about the feature development 🙂 

*In-app contact*

Ideally, similar to the process for drivers, we should change banking details only based on contact from the fleet portal. However, this is not yet rolled out globally and some countries still don’t have it (CZ, MX, PT, QA, SK, TH, TZ, UA)

*Other options*

For a less sensitive verification approach, we currently lack a standardized process for verifying the requester beyond contact from a verified channel. The additional questions we use make little sense, as individuals with access to the email or fleet portal could easily answer the verification questions as well.

Similarly, outgoing calls are hardly scalable; we would rely solely on phone calls to verify numbers instead of trusting verified emails. In my opinion, it’s the same level of verification, just via a different channel.

dfs = []

    files = os.listdir(folder_path)

        df['folder']=folder

First of all netting is not active in all markets due to legal/tax limitations hence if you compare totals across the globe they will not match. 

Second, VAT netting is active only for (private) Drivers. If you compare fleet-heavy markets the difference is big (e.g. RO, ES, PL). If you check markets where most of the drivers are privates the difference is smaller (e.g. Baltics).

Finally it depends on which exact measures you’re comparing against each other. As I mentioned in the previous ticket in the gmv explore the supply spend % is calculated using averages (average campaign bonus + average compensation + average manual compensation / average GMV). Also the different bonus components are with VAT. The small difference for the driver-based markets can be explained by this as the source of all data is the same between both reports

Correct, not every transaction includes VAT because not all drivers are VAT-liable. To see the net total we should always use values without VAT (but this doesn’t happen in the gmv view I’m afraid)

{quote}So do I understand correctly, that the difference is mainly driven by the fact that your dashboard includes the subtypes for private drivers only, while in GMV Explore dashboard we see private+fleets?{quote}

Correct

{quote}Also, I have a question regarding averages, the average of what is taken? if I look at monthly GMV or spend for a country, what do you mean by average (average of what period or a subtype?..){quote}

It depends on your filters. Let’s say you look at supply spend % of Poland for the last complete month (April 2024). The calculation fetches:

* average campaign bonus for the month in PL (total campaign bonus / number of rides)
* average compensation for the month in PL (total compensations / number of rides) 
* average manual compensation for the month in PL (total manual comps / number of rides) 
* sum the 3 above up to get the average driver bonus for the month in PL (average campaign bonus + average compensation + average manual compensations) 
* and compares this value with the average GMV (total GMV / number of rides) → average driver bonus / average GMV

The average doesn’t check the bonus subtypes, only based on period & location

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example,that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

*Your rights*

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,

the difference here is having the option available vs rejections on the ordering level. We do not oversee the RB as an available feature to choose but we do run checks for brand new companies immediately placing RB orders without accumulating reliable history first. 

_Why so_? Ridebooker is our weakest product in terms of fraud due to very limited information available about the customer and the company to do effective fraud prevention. End of last year, we were still allowing 'quick signup to ridebooker ordering' for the companies and this resulted in a total of 60K eur loss from one weekend due to the easy and fast flow that fraudsters find a sweet treat to misuse. We do have some improvements since then that can help prevent fraud better such as pre-authorisation checks and the option to keep the pre-authorised amount. Therefore we are open to discussing how to make the flow better for your big clients.

Hence, it would be very beneficial if you could describe further on what kind of steps you go through with these example companies - for us it is important on how to distinguish the good companies from irregular ones with the limited information at hand. *Have you noticed some data points that these super good clients have that we can rely on?* We are also reviewing this ourselves on where we can be more lenient or potentially target better but here you definitely have more information on the clients through communication. 

Long term we do have this potential idea of having a VIP business flag that local agents can apply in order to bypass fraud prevention friction - however - this potential solution still requires significant development and will not be prioritised due to low impact (in comparison to other product work needing to be done).

For example,that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

*Your rights* 



In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 



If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.





Yours sincerely,

Bolt

{noformat}import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns


def plot_distribs(n):
    # Set the aesthetic style of the plots
    sns.set(style="whitegrid")

    # Define the parameters
    #n = 30  # Sample size
    std_dev = 10  # Standard deviation
    differences = [2, 4]  # Differences between the means of the two distributions
    bins = np.linspace(-6, 6, 30)  # Define bin edges for histograms

    # Create the figure and axes
    fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 6), sharey=True)

    # Generate and plot histograms for each subplot
    for i, diff in enumerate(differences):
        mean_control = -2
        mean_treatment = mean_control + diff

        sampling_control = []
        sampling_treatment = []
        for _ in range(1000):
            samples_control = np.random.normal(mean_control, std_dev, n)
            sampling_control.append(np.mean(samples_control))
            samples_treatment = np.random.normal(mean_treatment, std_dev, n)
            sampling_treatment.append(np.mean(samples_treatment))

        # Plotting with seaborn for better aesthetics
        sns.histplot(sampling_control, bins=bins, ax=axs[i], kde=False, color="skyblue", label='Control', alpha=0.6)
        sns.histplot(sampling_treatment, bins=bins, ax=axs[i], kde=False, color="red", label='Treatment', alpha=0.6)
        
        # Add mean lines
        axs[i].axvline(np.mean(mean_control), color='blue', linestyle='dashed', linewidth=1)
        axs[i].axvline(np.mean(mean_treatment), color='red', linestyle='dashed', linewidth=1)
        
        mean_line_control = np.mean(sampling_control)
        mean_line_treatment = np.mean(sampling_treatment)
        axs[i].axvline(mean_line_control, color='blue', linestyle='dashed', linewidth=1)
        axs[i].axvline(mean_line_treatment, color='red', linestyle='dashed', linewidth=1)
        axs[i].set_title(f'Effect Size = {diff}, Sample Size = {n}', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
        axs[i].plot([mean_line_control, mean_line_treatment], [5, 5], 'k-', lw=2)  # Example height of 5, adjust as needed
        axs[i].text((mean_line_control + mean_line_treatment) / 2, 5, f'Diff = {diff}', horizontalalignment='center', verticalalignment='bottom')
        axs[i].set_xlabel('Outcome', fontsize=12)
        axs[i].legend()

    # Set common labels and title
    #axs[0].set_ylabel('Frequency', fontsize=12)
    #plt.suptitle(f'Sampling Distributions at Sample Size {n} with Different Effects', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')

    #plt.show()
    filename = f'giffy/ab_test_{n}.png'
    plt.savefig(filename)
    plt.close()
    frames.append(filename)
    
import imageio
frames = []
for x in range(50,500,50):
    plot_distribs(x)

gif_path = 'ab_test_animation.gif'
with imageio.get_writer(gif_path, mode='I', duration=0.5) as writer:
    for filename in frames:
        image = imageio.imread(filename)
        writer.append_data(image)

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import imageio

def create_frame(x, y, x1, y1, x2, y2, color='green', alpha=1.0):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    # Custom background and removing frame lines
    ax.set_facecolor('#f0f0f0')
    for spine in ax.spines.values():
        spine.set_visible(False)

    # Plotting dots with a drop shadow effect
    shadow_x_offset, shadow_y_offset = 0.003, -0.003
    ax.scatter(x1 + shadow_x_offset, y1 + shadow_y_offset, color='gray', alpha=0.5)
    ax.scatter(x2 + shadow_x_offset, y2 + shadow_y_offset, color='gray', alpha=0.5)
    ax.scatter(x1, y1, color='blue', edgecolor='navy', linewidth=0.5, s=50)
    ax.scatter(x2, y2, color='red', edgecolor='darkred', linewidth=0.5, s=50)
    if x is not None and y is not None:
        ax.scatter(x + shadow_x_offset, y + shadow_y_offset, color='gray', alpha=0.5)
        ax.scatter(x, y, color=color, edgecolor='black', linewidth=0.5, s=100 * alpha)

    ax.set_xlim(0, 1)
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
    ax.axis('off')  # Hide axes for cleaner animation
    fig.canvas.draw()
    image = np.frombuffer(fig.canvas.tostring_rgb(), dtype='uint8')
    image = image.reshape(fig.canvas.get_width_height()[::-1] + (3,))
    plt.close(fig)
    return image

# Increase the number of dots in each pile
num_dots = 1000
x1, y1 = np.clip(np.random.normal(loc=0.1, scale=0.045, size=num_dots), 0.01, 0.4), np.clip(np.random.normal(loc=0.1, scale=0.045, size=num_dots), 0.01, 0.4)
x2, y2 = np.clip(np.random.normal(loc=0.9, scale=0.045, size=num_dots), 0.6, 0.99), np.clip(np.random.normal(loc=0.1, scale=0.045, size=num_dots), 0.01, 0.4)

frames = []

# Simulate the falling and moving of the first dot
for y in np.linspace(0.9, 0.5, 30):  # Higher change point
    frames.append(create_frame(0.5, y, x1, y1, x2, y2))

# Move diagonally to the first pile
for x, y in zip(np.linspace(0.5, 0.1, 20), np.linspace(0.5, 0.2, 20)):
    frames.append(create_frame(x, y, x1, y1, x2, y2, color='blue'))

# Simulate the falling and moving of the second dot
for y in np.linspace(0.9, 0.5, 30):  # Same higher change point
    frames.append(create_frame(0.5, y, x1, y1, x2, y2))

# Move diagonally to the second pile
for x, y in zip(np.linspace(0.5, 0.9, 20), np.linspace(0.5, 0.2, 20)):
    frames.append(create_frame(x, y, x1, y1, x2, y2, color='red'))

Hi Alexander

1] To summarise our call

* AASA is our Business Client, currently governed by our generic BB T&C.
* AASA uses BB solution to book rides for its clients, including business clients representatives.
* Dotsure is one of such AASA business clients. It is not a Bolt client and we do not have a business relationship with them. AASA simply has a business account where they add the representatives of Dotsure as riders, similarly to other AASA business clients. Dotsure involvement should not be relevant for this case, and has nothing to do with the request of AASA.
* AASA wants to ensure SA POPIA compliance with Bolt, and sees Bolt as “_Supplier-Operator_”. (Internal - this is the equivalent of “processor” under the GDPR). They shared a template with us obliging Bolt to comply with their conditions on personal data processing (internal - the conditions are similar to the requirements under Art. 28 of GDPR for processors).

[~accountid:5f1fbb0eef11df002588080f] please confirm the summary above.

2] Now, with regard to the agreement they shared. I was able to complete the review today.

The agreement is not acceptable, and has numerous provisions which we simply could not comply with. Examples:

_1] 9.3.8.1 - “Bolt shall not share, transfer, disclose or otherwise provide access to the AA Personal Information to any third party”_

_2] 9.2. “PI and any associated records received by or compiled by or processed by the Supplier-Operator by virtue of its relationship with the AA and its scope of work, shall at all times remain the sole property of the AA and the Supplier-Operator shall comply with all lawful and reasonable instructions of the AA in respect of how this PI and any associated records shall be dealt with”_

_3] 9.4. “The Supplier-Operator shall be solely responsible for its employees and the third parties who it engages and who may have access to PI in order to perform its functions in terms of its engagement with the AA._ *_In this regard, the Supplier-Operator shall advise the AA of such arrangements and the AA reserves the right to approve such arrangements_*_.”_

_4] 9.5. “The Supplier-Operator shall maintain and securely retain all PI and related records as required by law for the requisite period and/ or the period determined by the AA.”_

_5]. 10.3. “Upon the AA’s request, the Supplier-Operator shall certify to the AA that all AA Personal Information in its (including its subcontractors’) possession or control has been returned or destroyed.”_

_6] 9.3.7.1. “The Supplier-Operator must process PI only with the knowledge or authorisation of the AA.”_

*The basic problem comes down to the following* - Bolt cannot accept the status of _Supplier-Operator under POPIA and subsequent stringent obligations that AASA wants to impose. Being a “Supplier-Operator”_ will _not correctly reflect Bolt`s current business model. Bolt considers itself a separate data controller under the GDPR - which corresponds to the status of “_responsible party” under the POPIA.

My next steps would be - i) confirming the summary with you; ii) aligning with Alon on the topic; iii) preparing a pushback message for AASA. If the pushback is not initially successful, we can plan a call with them, but I do not see this as strictly necessary now.

Hi all

I have reviewed the MasterCard DPA. The DPA is very comprehensive but raises compliance concerns in a few instances.

Most significant issues are:

1] *The DPA does not offer a readily available list of sub-processors* - such details are only available upon written request.

To ensure our compliance, we must request such list of sub-processors.

*2] Use of Data for MasterCard’s Own Purposes:* MasterCard is permitted to process personal data for its own service improvement and development as a data processor.

Ideally, for such activities which are clearly not necessary to allow Mastercard process data on behalf of Bolt, Mastercard must take up the role of a data controller. 

3] *Deletion or Return Personal Data.* The DPA requires written request to delete or return Personal Data by Bolt, whereas it must be automatic after termination of cooperation with the Bolt (as per our internal guidelines, after 3 months since the termination of cooperation).

In addition to the above, the DPA is mostly not compliant with our DPA standard. Specifically - i) audit split costs not specified; ii) conditions to assist Bolt with DPIAs, supervisory authorities requests not specified (only general wording); iii) data subject request response timelines not specified; iv) general and not specific authorisation of sub-processors; etc.

*Overall, there is nothing critical that would be a total red flag - but we need the list of their sub-processors to be included.*  [~accountid:712020:822a759a-daf0-4161-afbf-8b79a2985fba] we must request Mastercard to provide us with the list of sub-processors (ideally, appended to the Main Agreement).

I would definitely try to negotiate the DPA as its strict towards Bolt and relaxed toward Mastercard, but I understand there is not much room for negotiations and those are standard terms.

Hey [~accountid:619df38fc75da8007295630e], thanks a lot for this!

I have a couple of questions:

* have we thought about any ways of +*informing*+ *the persons who have been added as trusted contacts*?
** To give you a bit more context, we are obligated to inform the persons whose data we have and use. The only exception where we could avoid informing them is if we could prove that it’s objectively impossible for us to inform them. Having in mind that we have their phone number, it would be impossible to use the argument that “we didn’t have the person’s contact details, therefore, it is unable to inform them”.
** Having this in mind, would it be possible to, for example, send an SMS saying “_X added you as a trusted contact on Bolt, please press here to object_”? This is just a suggestion about how this could be done, I’m happy to hear about other options.
* have we thought about the ways of +*removing, changing the phone number*+ in case the person does not want to be added as a trusted contact?
** Having in mind that the collection method for this data is very particular (i.e. that we don’t collect the data directly from the person), we need to think through how do we ensure the data subject rights they have under GDPR, i.e. - right of access (right to get a copy of their data), right to erasure (right to delete their data and be removed upon request), etc.
* what I didn’t seem to understand is how this project correlates with the current stats we have:
** Call success rate is 66% now. If the riders who are aware that this might be Bolt who is calling and they might be in trouble at the time of the call don’t answer, why do we expect a random person to answer the call? 
* Do our friends have this feature?

In principle, it’s not impossible to launch the feature from privacy perspective, but we need to think of a way on how do we inform the persons, how do we enable them to have control over their data and how do we make sure they know and agree to their data being there.

I am more than happy to discuss this during a call.

* There are no other tables' long-running DDLs in the same MySQL instance. Debezium’s connector restart requires a MySQL global lock, which is usually acquired and not released by long-running DDLs (this is the issue with Prelive MySQL).
* The DAP Ingestion team can have the permissions to create test tables, alter and drop the test tables, and insert/update/delete rows from the test tables.
* Networking
** Between the MySQL instance and the Debezium Prelive EC2 instance
** Between the MySQL instance and DAP Ingestion team laptop VPN
* No master/slave is mandatory; we only need one small master instance and no slave to save on costs.
* We won’t generate lots of data, and long data persistence isn’t needed. DAP can take care of deleting the tables periodically.

Bolt increased the Agency Fee (Agreed Percentage) from 15% to 20% and notified the Partner about it by e-mail. The Partner states that it is not obliged to pay the increased fee, nor it is willing to terminate the contract as a result of the increase. It wishes to continue the cooperation with a 15% fee.

I have analysed this issue and in my opinion the Partner is right as there is no contractual basis for Bolt to increase the fee without Partner’s consent. Clause 13.5 of the T&C states that _Bolt reserves the right to update the General Terms anytime, by uploading the revised version on their webpage. Bolt will notify the Partner of any changes at least 30 days in advance. If the Partnerdoes not agree to the updated General Terms, it should be communicated to Bolt in order to terminate the Agreement and discontinue the use of the Bolt Food Platform._ However, the amount of the Agreed Percentage is not stiuplated in the General Terms but in the Agreement itself, therefore clause 13.5 does not apply to such change.

In my opinion, Bolt cannot expect the Partner to terminate the contract as it is contractually allowed to cover the fee of 15%. As a result, Bolt should either:
1. amend the agreement with the Partner (which taking into cosnideration Partner’s approach is rather not possible) or

2. terminate the contract itself.

I have several notes regarding the lawyer’s letter. We would need to clarify a few things (as the letter is very laconic). 

+First+, we should do an internal check regarding the Fleet mentioned in the letter and see if any issues turn up: is the Fleet still active, has their account been terminated (if yes, then for what reason; if no, then are there any other issues connected to them)?

+Second+, while we are doing this internal check, we should ask the lawyer for a deadline extension. The idea is to draft a response to the lawyer and explain that we would need to investigate this claim, but they would need to provide us with additional information and time. The more information we ask, the more likely they are to grant the deadline extension.

I suggest using the following keypoints when drafting the response to the lawyer:

# To stay civil, we should first thank them for addressing this matter and assure them that Bolt takes such claims seriously and means to find a solution that satisfies all parties.
# However, as in the letter there are several aspects not mentioned, Bolt would first need to conduct an internal investigation as to the background of their claim.
# For this purpose, the lawyer should provide Bolt with the following: 
(i) What is the claim based on exactly? If it is based on rides completed by the Fleet, they would need to provide Bolt with  references to the exact rides (with date and time etc), or at the very least the timeframe when the disputed rides were completed; 
(ii) What is the size of the Fleet’s claim? The letter only mentions the size of the lawyer’s claim. Therefore they should provide Bolt with the exact size of the claim in euros.
(iii) Where has the Fleet directed their requests to? The letter mentions “several requests” and we should ask the lawyer to provide Bolt with said requests (e-mails, screenshots etc.), so that Bolt can assess if the requests have been submitted and processed correctly.
The above information would enable Bolt to first fact check if (A) the Fleet has indeed completed all rides in accordance with Bolt T&Cs and guidelines; and (B) if the Fleet has indeed not been paid. If the above is true, Bolt can investigate if the Fleet has not been paid for a reason (for example Bolt has legally withheld payment due to a breach of the Fleet) or if it is indeed an error on Bolt’s side (whether technical or human).
# Regarding the lawyer’s costs, we should ask why are they invoicing this to Bolt, as they have not provided any services to Bolt.*
# The letter is addressed to [germany-drive@bolt.eu|mailto:germany-drive@bolt.eu] which (if I am not mistaken) is not the official contact address which Fleets use to communicate with Bolt. However, as the claim is clearly from a Fleet, it must be connected to Rides vertical and not Bolt Drive. We can ask the lawyer why did they address the letter to this address and not via an official communication channel used by Fleets-Bolt.**
# Only when the lawyer has provided Bolt with all of the above information and explanations can Bolt provide them with a substantive response to the claim (and a decision whether Bolt will make the payment or not).
# *Taking into account the volume of the information Bolt needs from the lawyer and also the volume of investigation needed to conduct by Bolt, the deadline set for May 13 is not feasible. Therefore, Bolt asks for an extension of the deadline to 14 business days*** starting from the date when the lawyer has provided Bolt with all information needed for Bolt to conduct its investigation.*
# If the lawyer does not respond to Bolt by May 13, Bolt shall assume that the lawyer and Fleet have withdrawn their claim.****

_*It seems that they mean for Bolt to reimburse the Fleet for the costs it has incurred as regards to the lawyer’s services, but since they have not spelled it out themselves, we should point this out to them and ask for an explanation. This also indicates that Bolt does not automatically agree to pay said costs._

_**It may be that this is simply an error on their end and it might not have any legal effect to their claim. However, as Bolt T&Cs specify the e-mail address meant for Fleets, they should either admit the error or try to explain why an essentially random e-mail was used._

_***You can set a different number of days here, however 14 seems reasonable to me._

_****_+_This last part may be somewhat risky_+_, as it is possible that their claim really does have a basis and if Bolt will not make any payments by their deadline they may pursue further legal action. However, they have not mentioned in their letter what are the consequences of Bolt not meeting the 13 May deadline (usually such letters of claim have this included) and it may be that they have not thought about it either. In any case, I believe adding the last part is a business decision._



Let me know if you have any questions regarding the above or wish to discuss something in more detail - I am happy to help.

Bolt is not a party to this agreement and therefore would not bear liability for its breach by the partner.

In each case in accordance with clause 13.3 Bolt would notify a partner about such amendment in advance so the partner can decide if they wish to accept the amended terms and continue the cooperation.

I will query the data for September/October period. And I will use the following two variables for making a choice about which threshold to use in fraud rules later on (after profiling itself is updated accordingly). Analysis data is saved to dbt_andreas_latt_spark schema.

*threshold user fraud rate* (total TP rate) - info in "{{threshold .. fraud rate}}" columns are aggregated to have fraud rate IF this threshold were chosen. 

*user_fraud_rate_bin* (bin TP rate) - Columns like "{{..._fraud_rate_bin"}}  are looking at thresholds ONLY in this BIN's data.



Two variables which showed promising results were {{avg_campaign_coverage_30d}} (better results, will start from this) and {{deleted_ratio_30d}}(will maybe add extra rules based on this later).



Analysis based on {{avg_campaign_coverage_30d}}:

*threshold user fraud rate*/*Total TP rate* is the preferred metric for choosing best rule & threshold, but it can be slightly misleading when used alone - case in point from October data, 0.55 threshold has really good overall TP of 71%, but that same bin’s data’s TP rate is only 40%, suggesting that it might actually be better to use 0.6 as a threshold.

Assuming that Bolt notified the Partner of the above change and the Partner did not diasagree with the update, it shall be deemed as accepted.

Pursuant to the current point 6.2 of the latest (above) version of T&C *_Bolt may, at its sole discretion, change the Agency Fee from time to time on 30 days  prior written notice to the Partner_*_._ *_If the Partner does not want to be bound by the revised Agency Fee, it may terminate the Agreement on 30 days written notice to Bolt and before the revised Agency Fee comes into effect._* _If the Partner issues a notice of termination of the Agreement before the revised Agency Fee comes into effect, it shall not be bound by the revised Agency Fee notwithstanding that the effective date of termination of the Agreement is after the proposed effective date of the revised Agency Fee._ *_In the absence of a termination notice, Partner shall be deemed to have accepted the revised Agency Fee._*

T&Cs are governed by the law of Estonia (point 13.7 of primary T&Cs or 13.8 of the latest ones) where an e-mail is considered as written form.

As a result of the above, Bolt was entitled to change the Agency Fee (provided that it notified the Partner of the change of T&C).

+*NOTE TO SELF*+ 

* AB had a call with [~accountid:6140b8db805a97006aa66cc8] on this matter on 9 May 2024 at 2.30pm. 

+*SUMMARY OF THE ISSUES*+ 

* Fraud Team have flagged habitual patterns with Drivers that they are not picking up passengers, starting the trip, driving a short distance and then completing the trip. This then results in the passenger being charged the full fare and the driver being paid out the full fare even though the trip did not occur. Bolt then has to refund passengers for the trip, which is resulting in a loss for the business. 
* The issue stems from the fact that Bolt do not recalculate downward during trips, however Bolt will recalculate upwards (for example: when a passenger adds another stop during a trip Bolt can calculate upwards, however if a passenger gets out early than expected Bolt cannot recalculate upwards). 
* [~accountid:6140b8db805a97006aa66cc8] highlighted that previously he has been informed by the UK legal team that Driver must receive the minimum fare that is presented to them on the acceptance screen and this is why the Ops team have never recalculated downwards. 
* This is costing the business money and is also not a good experience for passengers as they are making complaints to CS for refunds because of a poor customer experience. 
* The Fraud Team at Bolt want to put some rules in place which will stop this behaviour from occurring. To battle the number of trips that did not happen, to decrease refunds, they have the ability to downwards calculate to 0. 
* The Fraud Team anticipate that this would account for around 4,000 trips a month, would save around 35k in refunds. 
* NOTE: Calculating downwards in this scenario would only be applicable for ghost rides and not for any other circumstance e.g. passenger getting out early. 

+*AIM IS TO IMPROVE THE FOLLOWING*+ 

* Estimate: Prevent around 4000 rides where this happens.
* Money:  Save around circa 35k a month. 
* Great for the profits in the UK 
* Improves the experience for Bolt Business users as this has been flagged as an issue which may result in Bolt Business losing customers. 
* Better user experience for passengers. 
* Tightened up Bolts fraud rules.

Hey,

That’s because their commission amount is negative for these months, meaning we don’t have any commission to invoice.

This happens when driver’s compensations/campaigns are more than their commission. Since we deduct their compensations/campaigns from their commission, in that case they don’t have any commission to invoice.

The invoice is generated once their commission once again exceeds their compensation/campaign sum. Then this invoice would cover the whole period without an invoice.

Hello [~accountid:62ea2a695111209f4fde8265], sorry for the late reply. I was on sick leave and Carlos has been helping to check the discrepancy. Several things I want to highlight before we dive into the details:

# Balance logic has been changed on 2023-04-03, thus you may see different terms but include similar data. For example, app-payment means in-app payment + tips in old admin, which we no longer use it after 2023-04-03.
# Looker time period filter mistake. When filtering the date, Looker uses {{between}} slightly different from SQL. You need to use 2023-03-01 to 2023-07-01 to include 2023-06-30, as it will filter until *before the date* you query.
# Carlos has generated [this spreadsheet|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1kd6bzmLX64hPGo_IHiJ_UZjNZkh2Eu0VLZPwXzNH8wE/edit#gid=803049757] to check the details, the balance data matches with [this Look|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/dashboards/16966?Country+Code=hu&Balance+Local+Date=2023%2F03%2F01+to+2023%2F07%2F01&Currency=&City=&Transaction+Type=&Entity+Type=-NULL&Entity+ID=4207432%2C4207591%2C4252706%2C4252936%2C4276613%2C4295398%2C4381798%2C4389796%2C4397208%2C4420401%2C4424701] when including 06-30. 

Here is the further explanation of the reports:

* Difference of 1.75M between “1. ride fee per balance report” and ride report? tips are only 230k, why?

ride_fee is used only in new admin logic, while in the past app_payment includes all in-app ride_fee + tips. Also, ride_fee only contains in-app payment rides price, while you compare with ride report, you need to include cash payment as well. If you want to make the numbers match, then app_payment + ride_cash_payment + ride_fee = total rides price(sum with vat) + tips.

* What does “3. app-payment” per balance report mean?

app-payment is the term used in old admin, which includes total ride price from app payment + tips. Starting from 2023-04-03, Balance started to record tips separately.

* Difference of 538K between “7. ride_cash_payment” per balance report and cash rides per ride report, why?

ride_case_payment has been introduced to Balance since the balance structure has changed on 2023-04-03. In Old Admin we don’t record ride_cash_payment, thus the number doesn’t match.

* Reason why no bonus/campaign (2.5M - sum of 2. & 5. per balance report) was shown on the commission invoice?

Commission invoice has already deducted bonus/campaign. Taking driver_id = 4424701 as an example, the total fee is 525,355, bonus = 84,305, and in commission report the total amount is 441,049.60. I don’t know what’s the reason of hiding bonus information on the invoice, you can asking billing ops for more information.

* Per balance report, 2. bonus + 5. campaign + 6. fee = 6.38M, different from commission report (6.58M), can you have a look why?

This is because the time filter is wrong as mentioned above. You can check the Fees section in the new spreadsheet, that total Balance fees - (Balance Bonus + campaign) has a discrepancy of 86k with Total Commission invoice. This 86k discrepancy is because the bonuses given on 2023-06-29 and 2023-06-30 were not included, and credited to the next month invoice. 

* No Refund was shown on balance report, why?

The only refund record happened on 06-30, which in the previous report you didn’t include it. If you set the filter to from 2024-03-01 until before 2024-07-01, it shows up.



Hope this answered all your questions and if you have any additional questions, please feel free to ask, thanks.

We should not reissue any invoice upon request for the reasons like no NIP number at the time of issuance and a rider providing the number later, or a rider requesting a change of address or name later on. It is not allowed by the VAT law to reissue invoices for these reasons.

Unless it is our mistake, e.g. the value, subject of the sale, or NIP number is wrongly stated by us, then we reissue the invoice. And we need to report VAT for the new invoice.

If a rider requests to reissue the invoice for their own benefit in the future, +you can tell them+ +*according to art., 106b ust. 6 VAT law in Poland*++, we are not allowed to do so.+

Hey team, coming back with the answers for [~accountid:62722e092db308007024a425] 's questions:

* *Which driver data will be visible to them of the drive*r*?*
The visible driver data is part of the following endpoints: profile, activity, and income.
* *Will they have access to the driver portal?*
The driver shares access to their app on a consent basis to facilitate data portability of the endpoints a Rollee's customer (usually a lender) has requested to verify. Those endpoints are information profile, activity, and income.
* *Is the access limited to the driver activity and invoicing part of our systems?*
The portability concerns profile, income information (not necessarily the invoices), and activity. Rollee's customers are mainly earned wage access, auto finance, and consumer lending companies for gig workers, and they require a holistic view of their income and activity.
* *Do they have access to trip data and driver history?*
We have access to some trip data that helps structure the activity endpoint. Some information on trip data doesn't concern the driver's activity and is not treated. For instance, the number of trips per hour/day/week or the driver's preferred slots help to build a driver's risk profile for lending. The driver's history collected depends on our customers' scoring rules. The driver can authorize the share of 1, 3, 6, or 12 months of history, depending on the service they subscribe to. As a reminder, Rollee is a B2B Infrastructure embedded into their customers' onboarding. That means they don't offer specific products to drivers, but their customers do.
* *By using the credentials of the driver will they have any kind of access to rider data?*
We don't have access to it if you mean accessing real-time information about incoming trips or drivers' rider decisions. The information we access is past income and activity the driver wants to share with our customers for a specific service.
* *Do you have any kind of screenshots or examples how the display and dashboard of Rollee will look once the driver has connected their service with ours?*
The output we'll provide to Bolt will be a spreadsheet to start and will lead to a Dashboard view in the near future (It's on our product roadmap)
* *To which exact data will Rollee have access from Bolt?*
We'll provide Bolt with Market Insights (detailed in the contract), which we structure as we operate as a data controller for our income verification service. As part of the Deal with Bolt, we aim to become Bolt's partner to empower the fleet and financial ecosystem for Bolt drivers and riders.

* *Correct me if I’m wrong, but it doesn’t seem like a tool that we will use to validate the driver’s identity. We have other tools in place, such as document checks, driver selfie verification feature.*
* *What do you mean by identity validation?*
* *Why would we need to validate the drivers' income? To my understanding, their income should be = what they earn on our platform. What kind of validation do we need here?*

Drivers and, more generally, gig workers work with multiple platforms to generate revenues. The income verification process differs from traditional employees, who must provide income proofs from various entities during the credit process. Structuring their income and putting the proper context on their activity for lenders is painful for them. Rollee allows any self-employed person to consolidate their income from any platform thanks to their embedded link lenders can use. As a reminder, their service is not for drivers but for lenders, insurance, or real-estate companies to increase their acceptance rate for gig workers.

Important to distinguish - Bolt will not be using Rollee’s services to validate drivers identity. This is the connection between drivers <> Rollee <> lenders. What Rollee will be providing for Bolt is market intelligence based on earnings and activity of these drivers, in order for us to understand where we stand in terms of driver value proposition compared to our competitors (how much our drivers are earning compared to competitors, how much bonuses competitors are paying them, what’s their average ride price, how many trips per hour they’re doing and so). They will provide basically averages for the drivers in their pannel, and we won’t be able to identify drivers based on this data.

HI

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active). So actual commission invoice will never match with report.

Basically:

Commission invoice - the final sum of commission that  shows for the monthly period, how much commission we took from the driver in the end (after refunds, some of their bonuses/compensation, and rider discounts have been deducte- so this is Driver’s expenses this done to decrease Driver’s commission in the end.

But report and app expenses, shows gross amount that that driver owes to us before we deduct refunds/bonuses/compensations/ ride discounts. 

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].
