Hi [~accountid:712020:548c71a6-d1f4-404d-9c5e-482bc0de371a] 

To summarise:

1] In Germany, we are launching a promotional activity for Bolt “Formula Bolt”.

2] The activity is the following:

* We will monitor drivers providing services, and based on their positive or negative behaviour (finished, cancelled trips, etc) they will be assigned points. The driver stats are already collected by us, they will simply be utilised for a new purpose.
* With the points, they can win prizes for themselves and the Fleet Partners they represent.
* There are no negative consequences for drivers nor fleets, and nothing changes for them.
* Everyone would be able to check their progress on a specially created web page. Pseudonyms will be used to display the progress for a specific driver. The pseudonym will only be know to the driver - so no personal data is revealed to the public.

More information on the activity is in the ticket description and the presentation.





The activity will commence as follows:

1] Fleet Owners in Germany get reached out (a handful that we picked, not all of them), informed of the campaign, and automatically opted in to participate - they can object and opt out if they want to.

2] Drivers belonging to the fleets will be chosen to participate based on the criteria established by Bolt - upon the agreement to participate by the fleet, all drivers of the fleet could be opted in, taking into account criteria established by Bolt.

3] Drivers will be able to opt out - but will be automatically opted in based on the decision of the fleet to opt in - as they are representing the fleet. As said above, nothing will change for the driver and they do not have to provide any data to us - we are already collecting this via the App.

4] Based on the stats and the logic developed by Bolt, drivers and fleets can win prizes. 

Action points from privacy and legal:

1] Developing T&C for the campaign concerning both drivers and fleets - in my POV, this can be a single document.

2] I believe we can use our standard Campaign T&C template and update it. I will be able to support with the privacy section.

3] The privacy T&C section will have to be developed. As I see it, the most important part would be - a privacy notice informing the drivers and fleet owners about the activity and providing GDPR details such as their privacy rights. Additionally, because factually the fleet owners decision enrols also the driver to the campaign, a short disclaimer that Bolt and the fleet owner act as joint data controllers for the activity, and some supplementary details. No data transfer will commence - all of the data is already in Bolt`s possession.

4] As I envision, some disclaimers on privacy and T&C will have to be added to the comms received by the fleets and drivers within the campaign.

Hi[~accountid:712020:5c3f18cd-53ab-40ca-9fae-fb38035ab6d8],

In my opinion Art. 11 section 1 point 12 of the Act of October 12, 1990 on the Border Guard is not a valid legal basis which *obliges* Bolt to disclose any information, therefore Bolt may (but is not obliged) to do so.

If you look at the bigger picture, point 11 of the regulation states that border guard +*may demand*+ assistance from public authorities and the authorities are +*obliged to provide such assitance,*+ while point 12 states that border guard +*may apply for*+ the assistance of business entities. In point 12 there is no reference to the obligation of the entity.

As a result, it seems that the wording of the provisions allows to argue that the entities requested to provide assistance are not legally obliged to do so.

Additionally, kindly note that the above approach is also noticeable in legal commentaries.

_Ustawy regulujące ustrój poszczególnych służb wyraźnie odróżniają uprawnienie do „żądania udzielenia niezbędnej pomocy” od instytucji państwowych, organów administracji rządowej i samorządu terytorialnego oraz przedsiębiorców prowadzących działalność w zakresie użyteczności publicznej od uprawnienia do „zwracania się” do pozostałych podmiotów o udzielenie niezbędnej pomocy. Za takim rezultatem wykładni przemawia kilka argumentów:_

_(a) po pierwsze, trudno inaczej racjonalnie uzasadnić użycie przez ustawodawcę w sąsiadujących jednostkach tekstu aktu normatywnego odmiennych zwrotów;_

Mowa w nich o „prośbie o udzielenie pomocy”. Brak tego warunku w przypadku podmiotu, od którego żąda się udzielenia pomocy. Ponadto trudno racjonalnie wytłumaczyć, dlaczego warunkiem wykonania obowiązku prawnego przez osobę, do której zwrócono się o udzielenie pomocy, byłoby wyrażenie przez nią na to zgody, a nie można założyć, że wskutek wydania rozporządzenia wykonawczego do ustawy doszło do uchylenia przewidzianego w niej obowiązku. _Należy więc przyjąć, że postanowienia rozporządzeń wykonawczych dopowiadają to, co można wywieść w drodze wykładni już z przepisów ustawy: osoba, do której zwrócono się o udzielenie pomocy, nie jest na mocy  ustaw ustrojowych prawnie zobowiązana do jej udzielenia._

+*Automated decision-making*+ 

*Rental services*

Our internal monitoring system tracks each event that occurs whilst a user is using the scooter, assigns it a certain weight, then calculates an overall score for reckless driving and issues a warning once the user reaches a certain score threshold. The total score of the user is the sum of the reckless events over the last five rides.

If we detect any potentially dangerous behaviour then we will issue the user with a warning in the app to encourage them to refrain from using the scooter in a certain way. There are three levels of warnings:

#  *first warning* - informs the user about the risks of misbehaviour;
#  *second warning* - limits the speed of the scooter until the overall user score improves; and
#  *third warning* - temporarily suspends the user from the service. The user is able to contest the suspension by contacting our Customer Support Team for further information as to why their account was suspended.

For safety considerations, we cannot disclose the exact thresholds that trigger our warnings to prevent users from abusing the system.

*Taxi services*

To balance the interests of Passengers and Drivers, if the average Rider Rating drops below a certain threshold (which differs per country), an automatic warning will be issued.  If the average Rider Rating is not improved within 90 days following a warning, a 6-month temporary suspension will be issued. This will be based on an automated decision but does not produce legal or similarly significant effects. 

You will get temporality suspended only if you appear (based on your average Rider Rating) to repeatedly:

* violate the Terms and Conditions for Passengers and Marketplace Conduct Guidelines for Riders; and 
* have a negative impact on Drivers' interests and the integrity of the Bolt Platform as a whole. 

The suspension only limits your ability to order a ride, and does not limit your access to the rest of the Bolt App, or to any other of our services.

*Safety Checks*

We may also use automated decision-making in order to undertake fraud checks which are necessary for us to perform our services, ensure that the services are paid for and ensure the protection of riders from fraudulent transactions on their payment cards.

*Verification*

We may use automated decision-making in order to verify you which is necessary to ensure the safety of our platform and the enforcement of our terms and conditions.

*Complaints*

We may also use automated decision-making for complaint resolution purposes. We may use the complaints information you provide to our customer support team via our chat function. The information relating to your complaints may be used to generate an automated response which will then be evaluated by a human agent to make the final decision.

*Human Intervention*

In cases where we use automated processing or profiling that has a significant effect on your rights, you have the right for human intervention and the right on grounds relating to your particular situation to object to the processing of personal data concerning you based on automated decisions/profiling, and to express your point of view and contest the outcome of the decision by contacting our Customer Support in our app. You may also be entitled to an explanation regarding the logic of making an automated decision.

Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws.

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

Agreement reached that business-billing will treat successfully requested cancel as processed cancel - hence the corner-case of missing event for failed payments (expired payments cron) in requested cancel state is not problem anymore.

Keeping the ticket open as payments system should be the only source-of-truth for payments status and details, ie. cancel requested shall not be interpreted as cancelled until there is an event/update from the payments system that says.

In this particular flow do payment system publish an event that’s consumed by two subscribers:

* bookings
* business-billing

If payments publish the failed event for payment in cancel request it currently causes issues to bookings, as they relate the provided booking id to an order and send failed payment info to rides, which always operate with one active booking only and cancel the order. That’s find if there was only one booking.

However in case of two bookings (scenario when end user tried to enter payment and failed, then they tried for 2nd time and succeeded). On the order side there is only one booking (the 2nd one), in bookings systems have two bookings (one in cancel requested state, interpreted as cancelled), payments have two payments (one pending authorisation, 2nd authorised), now when payments expire/fail the payment pending authorisation (for apple pay in 5 mins) and send failed payment event for the first payment (booking id) then bookings will cancel the whole order.

Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person.

breaking the problem down.

all data presented below are monthly averages between Jan/2023 and April/2024. 

* topping up to add money vs topping up to pay a debt:
** when users are paying debt:
*** avg CB count rate = 0.15%
*** avg CB amount rate = 0.46%
** when users are adding money (balance >= 0): 
*** avg CB count rate = 7.17%
*** avg CB amount rate = 9.16%
*** between Jan/24 and Mar/24 when we were attacked by resellers, the CB amount rate went to an avg of *30.2%*. 

if we look at users adding money that either:

* have 0 trusted payments
* or card_age == 0 
* or card_spending in the previous 30 days == 0 

then the CB amount rate goes as high as *55%*. 

top-ups are only open to all users in a limited amount of countries: BE, NL, CH, and IT. 

if we look at those countries, the CB rate went as high as *75% in NL in February 2024*. now resellers moved to BE, where the monthly volume for users adding money increased from 14k euros a month to over 54k. 20% of that volume in April already turned into chargebacks and more will arrive in the next weeks. 

solution:

* we’ll challenge users who are adding money that matches one of the three conditions mentioned above.

query used:

{code:sql}SELECT 
date(date_trunc('month',co.created)) AS MONTH,
--CASE WHEN CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.additional.payment.balance.amount_eur') AS REAL) >= 0 THEN 'adding_money' ELSE 'paying_debt' END AS balance_purpose,
APPROX_DISTINCT(co.id,0.0041) AS count_top_ups,
SUM(co.user_price_eur) AS sum_top_ups_eur,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN co.is_chargeback THEN co.id END,0.0041) AS count_cbs,
ROUND(CAST(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN co.is_chargeback THEN co.id END,0.0041)*1.000/APPROX_DISTINCT(co.id,0.0041) AS double),3) AS cb_count_rate,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN co.is_chargeback THEN co.fraud_loss/co.eur_currency_rate END) AS double),0) AS fraud_loss,
ROUND(CAST(ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN co.is_chargeback THEN co.fraud_loss/co.eur_currency_rate END) AS double),0)*1.000/SUM(co.user_price_eur) AS double),3) AS cb_sum_rate
FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co
LEFT JOIN archive_analytical.user_top_up_request d ON d.meta.order_id = co.order_id 
WHERE co.created_date >= date '2023-01-01'
AND co.order_type = 'top_up'
AND d.created_hour >= date '2023-01-01'
AND co.payment_method_type = 'processout'
AND CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.additional.payment.balance.amount_eur') AS REAL) >= 0
AND (CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.additional.payment.user_payments.successful_payments_trusted') AS bigint) = 0
OR CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.additional.card.card_age_in_days') AS bigint) = 0 
OR CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.additional.payment.user_cards_spending.month.payment_count') AS bigint) = 0)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 DESC{code}

Our third-party vendors and other service providers and contractors have access to your personal data to help carry out the services they are performing for us or on behalf of us. This may include vendors and providers who provide email or moreover electronic communication services, tax, legal and accounting services, product fulfilment, identity/verification processes, payment processing, customer support, fraud prevention and detection, data enhancement, web hosting and cloud storage, research, including surveys, analytics, crash reporting, performance monitoring and artificial intelligence, machine learning and statistical services. In addition, we will share data like your geolocation with Google in connection with the use of Google maps in our apps. 

+*Automated decision-making*+ 

*Rental services*

Our internal monitoring system tracks each event that occurs whilst a user is using the scooter, assigns it a certain weight, then calculates an overall score for reckless driving and issues a warning once the user reaches a certain score threshold. The total score of the user is the sum of the reckless events over the last five rides.

If we detect any potentially dangerous behaviour then we will issue the user with a warning in the app to encourage them to refrain from using the scooter in a certain way. There are three levels of warnings:

#  *first warning* - informs the user about the risks of misbehaviour;
#  *second warning* - limits the speed of the scooter until the overall user score improves; and
#  *third warning* - temporarily suspends the user from the service. The user is able to contest the suspension by contacting our Customer Support Team for further information as to why their account was suspended.

For safety considerations, we cannot disclose the exact thresholds that trigger our warnings to prevent users from abusing the system.

*Taxi services*

To balance the interests of Passengers and Drivers, if the average Rider Rating drops below a certain threshold (which differs per country), an automatic warning will be issued.  If the average Rider Rating is not improved within 90 days following a warning, a 6-month temporary suspension will be issued. This will be based on an automated decision but does not produce legal or similarly significant effects. 

You will get temporality suspended only if you appear (based on your average Rider Rating) to repeatedly:

* violate the Terms and Conditions for Passengers and Marketplace Conduct Guidelines for Riders; and 
* have a negative impact on Drivers' interests and the integrity of the Bolt Platform as a whole. 

 

The suspension only limits your ability to order a ride, and does not limit your access to the rest of the Bolt App, or to any other of our services.

We may also use automated decision-making in order to undertake fraud checks which are necessary for us to perform our services, ensure that the services are paid for and ensure the protection of riders from fraudulent transactions on their payment cards.

*Verification*

We may use automated decision-making in order to verify you which is necessary to ensure the safety of our platform and the enforcement of our terms and conditions.

*Complaints*

We may also use automated decision-making for complaint resolution purposes. We may use the complaints information you provide to our customer support team via our chat function. The information relating to your complaints may be used to generate an automated response which will then be evaluated by a human agent to make the final decision.

*Human Intervention*

In cases where we use automated processing or profiling that has a significant effect on your rights, you have the right for human intervention and the right on grounds relating to your particular situation to object to the processing of personal data concerning you based on automated decisions/profiling, and to express your point of view and contest the outcome of the decision by contacting our Customer Support in our app. You may also be entitled to an explanation regarding the logic of making an automated decision.

Discussed this ticket with Craig Brothers:
UK Ops are changing city for driver registration approx 40-50 per day.
Cause of this is due to regulatory requirements, lead can only be accepted in the city that issues their document confirming entitlement to drive, however lead registers in the city they intend to drive in.

Ops request that when changing City that a driver registration is linked to, the flow ID (and document set used, UK has different set for each city) for that city is changed to the flow (and document set) of the new city.

Ops will manually download documents from registration, change city, re-upload documents to registration (using the new document set), and then take needed action (changing registration to document resubmission needed, accepting registration, etc).

It is noted that this used to be how changing cities worked until the change to using config reg flow, as previously the document set for a registration was based solely off the city id on the registration. Using config reg flow it uses the document set for the reg flow instead.

Hello! Legal and Privacy reviewed the agreement. There are a few comments and suggestions from Legal side. Considering its a bank, this is for a short and specific period of time (1-2-3 months until ProcessOut /Mono is ready.  

*Legal review overview:*

By signing this agreement, Bolt agrees to the bank's terms and services, which include account opening, servicing, issuing of payment cards, internet banking, deposits and, fund transfers. The bank sets and can change the tariffs (fees) and rules for these services twice a month, but must notify their customers in advance. No chance to negotiate new fees. 

However, if Bolt doesn't agree with the changes, we have the right to terminate the agreement. 

Bolt also has the right to select the services they wish to receive and must sign an application for each service. The bank is obligated to provide the services as per the agreement, and the customer must pay for the services as per the tariffs. The bank reserves the right to amend the rules and tariffs in compliance with Ukrainian laws and regulations. Bolt does not have a say on it other that terminating the agreement.   

There are several risks for Bolt. These risks are primarily related to the terms of the agreement, the obligations of the Customer, and the rights of the Bank. 

Risks summary: 

# *Changes to Tariffs and Rules:* The *Bank reserves the right to modify the Tariffs* and the Rules governing the services provided under the agreement (clauses 4, 5). Such changes could potentially increase the costs of the services for Bolt or alter the terms in a way that may be less favorable. *Bolt is deemed to have accepted these changes unless it terminates the agreement before* the changes come into effect, which could disrupt its banking operations. 
#  *Direct Debit Authorization:* *Bolt authorizes the Bank to carry out direct debit transactions from its accounts*, including for the repayment of any debts or obligations to the Bank (clause 9). The Bank might execute debits at an inopportune time for Bolt, potentially affecting our cash flow management. 
#  *Currency Exchange Risk*: In the event Bolt lacks funds in the required currency, it authorizes the Bank to conduct currency exchanges to fulfill obligations, potentially at *unfavorable exchange rates* (clause 9). This could lead to increased costs due to exchange rate fluctuations and the Bank's discretion in determining the exchange rate *(not more than 10% deviation* from the official NBU rate, which is a LOT). 
# *Automatic Acceptance of Terms: Related to the first point above.* The structure of the agreement implies that Bolt, by continuing to use the Bank’s services, *automatically accepts any amendments to the Tariffs or the Rules* (clauses 4, 5, 7). 

What I think we should do: 
- we should push back on the bank's ability to change the tariffs and rules twice a month. This could potentially lead to frequent and unexpected cost increases for the services. 
- We should negotiate a limit on how often and by how much the bank can change the tariffs. Additionally, we should request that the bank provides ample notice for any changes, giving us enough time to decide whether to continue or terminate the service.

*From a Privacy perspective:*

But considering there is no time and we will drop them in 1-2 months, I do not really see a need in this. And honestly its so detailed and specific, that I do not think there is a chance to negotiate or bring it to our standards it even if we had time.”

h3. What will be the cost impact of this on my DWH?

In short, very little. There are 3 major aspects of DWH cost: storage, compute, and network egress.

* *Storage*: None. We don't store anything additional in your warehouse, so there are no extra storage costs.
* *Compute*: Low. We make highly efficient queries to extract data from your warehouse. To be extra careful, we recommend provisioning the smallest possible warehouse for use with Warehouse Connectors (eg: [+X-Small in Snowflake+|https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/cost-understanding-compute#virtual-warehouse-credit-usage]). If syncs run slowly with this size, you can scale up to trade compute cost for speed.
* *Network Egress*: Low. We only extract rows that have changed and leverage gzip compression to reduce bytes over the wire. Assuming an egress rate of $0.08 per GB and 100 compressed bytes per event, this is a cost of less than $0.01 per million events.

Summary:

1] The drivers who have completed their registration and created their profile can be reached out.

2] We can first reach via an email and insert a privacy disclaimer there, and if we did not get a response from the driver, we can follow up with them via a call. At the beginning of the call, we must state that:

i) Its made on behalf of Bolt, and the contact details were received when the driver signed up.

ii) The call is a survey, and specify the purpose (i.e. to learn more drivers experience in the market).

iii) If they ask, remind them that they were presented with a privacy notice detailing how Bolt processes personal data upon sign up, and that they received an email before with information about the survey activity, details how personal data is processed, and a link to the privacy notice.

Ideally, we would need a more comprehensive statement or explicit consent, but because of the markets and limited scope, the activity should be low risk. To ensure basic compliance, it's still important to provide the details above. 

3] The email disclaimer can be the following:

_“_You are being contacted by Bolt as you provided your contact details during the sign up as a driver_. We conduct this survey based on legitimate interest to learn more about your experience as a driver in [specify country/ies]. For details on how your data is processed by Bolt and your privacy rights, please refer to our privacy notices at: [_[_link to global_|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/] _or localised notice if available].”_

4] After the activity is completed, the team will delete identifying personal data from the responses and use only aggregate data for further analytics. Max period of 6 months for the personal data retention (identifiers).

During the 12 weeks after introducing the redesign we received *5,76% less tickets* than in the same period before (1129 vs 1064)

On W17 a large influx of tickets was received relating to a bug on the DA side, which skews the results:

* DA tickets increased by 9,68% (692 vs 759)
* DI tickets decreased by 30,21% (437 vs 305)

Due to the DA spike the results are inconclusive, however the DI reports showed a significant decrease in volume.

However, overall the results are not significant enough to warrant a success - a total decrease of 5,76%, though significant, will not allow the driverX team to focus on any side projects.

To double-check the impact of the SD redesign we will wait another 12 weeks *(until 16.07.2024),* but will start preparations for the next steps because spikes like these are common in driver apps and should be accounted for as a worst-case scenario.

There are multiple possibilities for next steps:

# Hire another person
# Use LLM to automatically sort, reject or redirect incorrect escalations
# Improve CS quality by working together with the CSKM team
# Allow only inhouse CS to send reports about driver apps

*Option #1 - hire another person*

Hiring should be used as a last resort not only because it costs the most money, but also because the job is not fulfilling and will not allow the person to grow in any meaningful way.

_Resolution: should only be used as a last resort._

*Option #2 - use LLMs to automatically sort, reject or redirect incorrect escalations*

This is a possibility, however it also costs money (less than hiring an FTE), requires implementation from the engineering side, time for training & double-checking for errors. Implementing this will take too much time - the team has already been struggling for months and a quicker solution is needed.

_Resolution: can be complimentary, but not viable as the main solution_

*Option #3 - improve CS quality by working together with the CSKM team*

Working with CS (CSKM Quality team, outsourced CS management) is a great way to support the already existing training & learning opportunities for CS, but is difficult due to the teams being overloaded and prioritizing other topics. The first review with CSKM Quality is planned for Q3’24, with possible results visible in Q4’24 and beyond, which is too slow to rely on fully.

_Resolution: can be complimentary, but not viable as the main solution_

*Option #4 - allow only inhouse CS to send reports about driver apps*

Over 80% of escalations to technical support is done by outsourced CS (Majorel, Teleperformance, Transcom and others; [source|https://taxify.atlassian.net/jira/servicedesk/projects/TECH/reports/custom/456/timescale/9?startTime=2024-01-01&endTime=2024-04-01&timeBreakdown=w]), who are not educated in driver topics well enough to understand the intricacies of the domain.

Even though the SD redesign was supposed to educate them *before* sending in a report to technical support (more info here: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TECH/pages/4720099398/Driver+apps+Service+Desk+Redesign|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TECH/pages/4720099398/Driver+apps+Service+Desk+Redesign|smart-link]), this did not have the desired effect, as can be seen from this analysis

The most efficient way to move forward would be to allow only the more experienced in-house CS (with direct managers who can be contacted in case of knowledge gaps) to escalate tickets to the driver apps team.

_Resolution: create a transition plan to allow only in-house CS to send technical support reports on driver apps._

Hi [~accountid:62e9498948e310e672955e85] See advice received from external counsel below: 



+*Executive summary*+

Counsel has considered Bolts potential legal exposure under the Equality Act 2010 (EqA) in respect of the allegations made by the Passenger. 

Counsel consider it possible that the passenger could make a successful argument that Bolt is liable for discriminatory acts of the driver (if these acts are found to have occurred as alleged). The recommendation is that Bolt consider settling the potential claim(s).  

+*Liability*+

Bolt would be considered a service provider under Part 3 of the Equality Act 2010. While the Passenger terms make it clear that drivers operate as independent contractors. If a court were to accept that model, Bolt may be able to argue that they are not jointly liable for the drivers’ actions (as they are not the driver’s employer). However, there is a risk that a court would not accept that the independent contractor model is reflective of the reality of the relationship between the driver and Bolt. The court may determine that the driver is in fact an employee (within the meaning of the EqA) and Bolt is therefore liable for the acts of the driver as their employer. 

Taking into account the current employment tribunal proceedings Bolt would want to defer from any further proceedings where the  employment status of drivers is challenged (particularly so if an adverse ruling were to be made).

Even if it was found that the driver is considered an independent contractor, Bolt may still be liable under the terms of the EqA for the acts of the driver as it’s “agent”. Given that Bolt recently accepted that it acts as principal in the provision of passenger journeys in the recent Tax Tribunal (in respect of London based drivers). It would therefore be difficult to argue that the same principal / agent relationship does not exist in respect of liability under the EqA, and Counsel would not recommend that any such argument be made as it may compromise the approach taken in the first-tier tax tribunal. 

Taking all the above into consideration Counsel consider it likely that Bolt could be deemed liable for the act of the driver in this case, especially given the matter would be litigated in the County Court were the judges will be less familiar with the intricacies and technical arguments associated with employment and discrimination law (and therefore may be more likely to rule in favour of a non-legally represented party if they believe there to be wrongdoing of some sort). 

Whilst the driver can also be personally liable for acts of discrimination under the EqA, it is likely that the potential claimant(s) would prefer to pursue Bolt given the Company will have deeper pockets than the individual driver. 

+*Financial exposure under the Equality Act*+

If a court did find Bolt liable for the alleged acts of the driver, then they could be ordered to pay damages which may include an injury to feelings award. 

Mrs Patel seeks £3,800 in injury to feelings, and a sum of £1250 in respect of the separate consumer rights claim.

Mr Patel seeks £2,000 in injury to feelings for direct / indirect discrimination plus a further £2,000 for victimisation. He also seeks a refund of the cost of the fare.

The main loss sought is in respect of injury to feelings. The precise level of an injury to feelings award is difficult to gauge as the courts have wide discretion when assessing this loss. It will depend on what is ultimately upheld and the subjective impact the events had on the claimant. The pre-action letter does refer, in particular, to the distress that the incident caused Mrs Patel. Taking the case at its highest, the sums sought (£7,800) are not unrealistic if the claims were to be successful.

Bolt will also incur time and costs in defending such an action and as the figures sought are not excessive, the legal costs will likely quickly outweigh the value of the claim. 

It is also worth bearing in mind that if the potential claimants initiate proceedings their expectations in respect of settlement could rise, and of course there may be cost implications depending on the outcome of any action. It may be that there is a window of opportunity now to try and resolve the matter for less than the sums currently claimed.

+*Recommendation*+

Counsel would not recommend that this is a case which Bolt would want to defend in a court setting and have provided two options on how Bolt can proceed: 

*Option 1* – send a short holding response to the potential claimants before 15 May simply noting that we are looking into this matter and will be in touch. Then issue a separate letter to the claimant with an initial low offer, of £500 - £1,000, to open settlement discussions and seek to anchor them at a low level. 

*Option 2* – send a short response in open correspondence to the potential claimant noting that in accordance with the Passenger Terms, drivers operate as independent contractors. We could then wait and see how the potential claimants respond as they may either (i) drop the matter (ii) issue a further letter restating their position or (iii) initiate legal proceedings. 

As highlighted above, it is worth bearing in mind that if the potential claimants initiate proceedings their expectations in respect of settlement could rise.
